headline: 澳洲藝術家的粉紅俗豔美學
context: 阿德雷德藝術家兼設計師史塔芙拉（Stavroula Adameitis），藝名 Frida Las Vegas，擅長棕櫚樹、粉紅貴賓犬、希臘石柱混搭的普普風俗豔美學，最新出版攝影集記錄澳洲式的通俗文化。

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Stavroula Adameitis, AKA Frida Las Vegas, is an Adelaide-based artist and designer known for her camp, pop art aesthetic. A typical work might feature palm trees, poodles, Greek pillars or bin chickens (Australian white ibises), sometimes all at once. Does it veer into kitsch? ‘I hope so,’ she says. ‘Nostalgia, colour and fun can be very energising, and the feeling we get from these objects in popular culture binds us together.’ The term kitsch comes from the German verkitschen, meaning ‘to cheapen’. In the 19th century it was deployed by elites to look down on the supposedly trashy vulgarity of art for the masses. ‘The idea still carries negative connotations,’ says Adameitis. In her new book, she invites us to stop sneering and start relishing Australia’s unparalleled genius for kitsch: ‘Good kitsch laughs with you not at you. It brings people along for the ride.’ Continue reading...
sources.title: Big things and pink poodles: Frida Las Vegas’s tour of Australian kitsch – in pictures

thread_text: 澳洲阿德雷德的藝術家史塔芙拉（Stavroula Adameitis），藝名 Frida Las Vegas，擅長把棕櫚樹、粉紅貴賓犬、希臘石柱通通混搭在一起，做出濃濃普普風的俗豔美學。她的新書邀請大家別再嫌棄「俗氣」，好好享受澳洲獨有的這種美感。目前這則消息只有《衛報》報導。
